title: fix: native subagent spawn recovers after shared Codex client replacement
body:
Closes #161051

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native subagent spawns being rejected as unavailable after another agent replaces the shared Codex app-server client, even though the account remains signed in.

## User Impact

Users can continue multi-agent delegation after follow-up turns without manually refreshing the model catalog. A genuinely unavailable account or runtime still fails closed. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The spawn choice can read a published native readiness observation from a retired client. On a native readiness rejection, it now asks the existing catalog owner for one renewed observation and re-evaluates the same admission gate, including current ownership. If the renewed catalog no longer lists the selected model, admission fails closed instead of falling through to a synthetic host entry. If renewal fails, the rejection names the renewal error instead of incorrectly suggesting that the account must be restored. The config-write/published-choice path remains unchanged and does not perform network discovery under the write lock.

## Evidence

- On the unchanged three-file final patch applied to `5d6f464a`, focused model-choice tests passed (37/37), covering stale readiness, one renewal per choice, automatic selection, configured runtime, owner replacement, removal from the renewed catalog, and the unchanged config-write path. Spawn tests passed (85/85) on the pre-final-guard candidate; they were not rerun after that guard. The new removal regression failed for both override and automatic selection without the guard (`resolved` instead of `unavailable`) and passed with it.
- On the final candidate, `tsgo:core` passed on `5d6f464a`; the `core-test-agents-root` type graph passed on the earlier `4f3a73d` base. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` (non-type-aware), and `git diff --check` passed for the three changed files on `5d6f464a`. The full `tsgo:test:src` suite was not rerun locally; CI remains pending.
- On the original `b580769` base, all 21 `tsgo:test:src` shards passed and targeted mutation checks made the new regressions fail when renewal, single-attempt behavior, or the owner-current check was removed.
- Measured local test wall time with `--maxWorkers=1`: model-choice 31 cases in 19.15 s and native model-choice 6 cases in 12.61 s. CI test timing is pending.
- The separate 3-second Codex login probe remains unchanged; worst-case renewal can still take approximately 5.5 seconds including model discovery.

## Final-commit remote verification (2026-09-29)

- [GitHub-hosted proof run](https://github.com/b4rRa/openclaw/actions/runs/36635014783) checked out the exact PR head `822594da0d12615a61f4208f24a95e8005bafe17`. The job container reported cgroup limits `CPU_MAX=200000 100000` (2 CPUs) and `MEMORY_MAX=4294967296` (4 GiB). This run did not build or test on the contributor's OpenClaw gateway.
- Focused model-choice files plus the temporary runtime probe: **39/39 tests passed** across 3 files. The probe executed the production `prepareModelChoice` and `resolveSubagentModelAndThinkingPlan` functions. For both explicit override and automatic selection, the synthetic native harness showed a fresh model choice resolving, a retired-client follow-up admitted by the spawn planner after one catalog renewal, and a genuinely revoked runtime rejected by the planner. The linked job log contains the `PROOF` and `SPAWN_PLAN` trace lines.
- **Scope limit:** this was a credential-free synthetic native-readiness probe, not an end-to-end Codex app-server/login run. No personal OAuth credential or private endpoint was sent to GitHub Actions. The earlier real Docker chain in #161051 was on a pre-final revision; this run specifically verifies the submitted SHA's choice and spawn-planning paths.
- Full upstream CI is still red in six underlying jobs involving UI E2E, SQLite/session storage, and Gateway tests; the aggregate CI gates reflect those failures. None of the failure traces names a changed file, but this is not proof that the PR cannot affect them.



## Maintainer real-Gateway verification (2026-09-30)

Verified unchanged head `822594da0d12615a61f4208f24a95e8005bafe17` in a secretless Node 24 Docker container. The Gateway and Codex plugin/app-server client were real built OpenClaw code; only the native stdio server and account/model responses were synthetic. No external inference or personal credentials were used. Two agents shared the mock native home, with explicit isolated profiles and state/database paths.

The sequence used `pnpm openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> agent` and native `item/tool/call` requests for **sessions_spawn**, not a direct import of the model-choice helper:

```text
Baseline 5029d1615d6093c31061480d2a89d01ebfbe3210:
  reviewer warm-up: SPAWN_READINESS_OK
  main native sessions_spawn: accepted
  same kept main session, follow-up native sessions_spawn:
    status=error
    The selected account or native runtime is unavailable ...
    Restore that account before spawning this model.

Candidate 822594da0d12615a61f4208f24a95e8005bafe17:
  reviewer warm-up: SPAWN_READINESS_OK
  main native sessions_spawn: accepted
  same kept main session, follow-up native sessions_spawn: accepted
  exact follow-up child: status=done; assistant=SPAWN_READINESS_OK

Revocation control on candidate:
  mock login unavailable and account/read returns no account;
  subsequent sessions_spawn admission: status=error, native runtime unavailable
```

The follow-up child was `agent:reviewer:subagent:4b6d1794-ddea-4dd5-9398-2125b28992cb`; its persisted assistant reply was checked independently after shutdown. A spawned child's reply was also retrieved through the Gateway's HTTP `sessions_history` tool. The mock is not a real Codex inference server, and this does not claim live account sign-out propagation: changing the mock account file alone did not revoke a still-current observation; the subsequent admission after that observation's lifetime ended was rejected.

Focused regression proof in the same isolation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/model-runtime-choice.test.ts src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **37/37 passed**, 51.37 s Vitest wall time.
- Keeping the contributor's tests but replacing only `model-runtime-choice.ts` with the unfixed baseline: both native recovery cases (override and automatic) **failed**, receiving `unavailable` instead of `resolved` (33.24 s). The exact candidate source was restored afterward.
- Candidate `pnpm build:docker` passed. The supported CLI wrapper additionally built the local plugin distributions before starting the Gateway.

No additional production change was needed; b4rRa's original fix and commits are preserved. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes on the three changed files. Existing upstream CI failures have not been rerun or claimed unrelated merely from their filenames.
